docs.title: Debug a RISC-V core over two pins.
docs.text:
An Arm Serial Wire Debug front-end for VexRiscv and VexiiRiscv, merged upstream and driving the same RISC-V DebugBus the JTAG DTM already uses. The Debug Module and the CPU are unchanged.

Funded by NLnet NGI0 Commons Fund · grant 2025-02-159

01 · Why this exists

docs.title: The ratified debug specification defines only a JTAG transport.
docs.text:
JTAG needs TCK, TMS, TDI and TDO, plus TRST where a reset line is wanted. Serial Wire Debug needs SWCLK and SWDIO. On a pin-constrained ASIC or a small FPGA board those two or three pins are contested, and on-chip debug is usually what gets cut.

Adding SWD to the RISC-V Debug Specification was requested and never adopted, so Raspberry Pi shipped it as a custom Debug Transport Module, which the specification explicitly permits. This project takes the same route for the VexRiscv family, in the open, under the upstream licences.

Stated precisely

This implements the RISC-V Debug Specification with a custom SWD transport. It is not an unqualified conformance claim, because no ratified version of the specification defines an SWD DTM. Describe it that way in any brief or datasheet.

riscv-debug-spec issue #785 tracks the original request.

02 · At a glance

docs.title: What changes
docs.text: A new transport front-end: wire-level PHY, SW-DP register file, and a DMI gateway with clock-domain crossing. Two pads instead of four or five.

docs.title: What does not change
docs.text: The Debug Module and the hart. Both are transport-agnostic in the specification, so a core that already has spec-compliant debug needs no redesign.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
Stock GDB behaviour. Halt, examine registers and memory, set breakpoints, single-step, load code, all over an off-the-shelf CMSIS-DAP probe.

03 · Requirements

docs.title: What a RISC-V processor needs to implement a debug interface.
docs.text:
Seven layers. Layers 2 and 3 are transport-agnostic, which is the reason adding SWD meant writing a front-end rather than touching the core.

01

docs.title: Debug Transport Module
docs.text:
Converts a wire protocol into Debug Module Interface reads and writes. The specification defines a JTAG DTM with IDCODE, dtmcs and dmi registers, and permits custom transports.

Element Need Note DMI master required Address, data, read/write op, busy status for backpressure Clock-domain crossing required The probe clock is asynchronous and intermittent. It stops when the probe idles, so the CDC cannot assume a free-running clock Error and retry semantics required The host must distinguish "busy, retry" from "failed"

02

docs.title: Debug Module
docs.text:
A DMI slave holding the debug register file. Without at least one of a Program Buffer or System Bus Access, a debugger can read registers but not memory.

Element Need Note dmcontrol required dmactive, haltreq, resumereq, ndmreset, hartsel dmstatus required allhalted, anyhalted, allrunning, allresumeack, authenticated hartinfo, abstractcs, command, data0..N required Abstract command interface and its data registers Access Register command required Minimum viable command set: GPR and CSR read and write Program Buffer progbuf one of two Feeds instructions to the halted hart; the usual route to memory access System Bus Access one of two sbcs, sbaddress, sbdata. Bus master that reaches memory without halting abstractauto optional Autoexec on data access. The difference between tolerable and glacial block download Authentication authdata optional Needed on production parts; see layer 06

03

docs.title: The hart
docs.text:
The layer most often underestimated. Debug Mode is a distinct operating mode above M-mode, with its own entry paths, register set and exit instruction.

Element Need Note Debug Mode required Operating mode above M-mode dcsr, dpc required Debug control and status, saved PC dscratch0, dscratch1 with progbuf Scratch for program-buffer execution Halt entry paths required haltreq, ebreak, trigger fire, step completion, halt-on-reset Park loop required A debug address region the hart enters on halt, where it spins and executes abstract commands Redefined ebreak required In Debug Mode it returns to the park loop instead of trapping dret required Exit from Debug Mode step, stopcount, stoptime required Single-step, and freezing counters and timers while halted

04

docs.title: Trigger Module
docs.text:
Optional in the specification. Without it there are no hardware breakpoints, which means no breakpoints in ROM or flash and no watchpoints. Each trigger costs comparator area, which is why implementations ship two to four rather than sixteen.

Element Need Note tselect, tdata1..3, tinfo optional Trigger register interface Address or data match trigger optional mcontrol class. The minimum for a usable hardware breakpoint

05

docs.title: Reset
docs.text:
Element Need Note ndmreset required Resets the system but not the Debug Module hartreset optional Per-hart reset Halt-on-reset resethaltreq in practice required The only way to debug from the first instruction. Frequently omitted, then missed during boot bring-up Transport reset required SWD has no reset wire. Recovery is the line-reset sequence on SWDIO: at least 50 clocks high, then idle cycles

06

docs.title: What the SoC integrator must provide
docs.text:
The layer where SWD diverges from JTAG, and the one to settle before committing to a hardened flow.

Element Need Note Two pins required SWCLK and SWDIO Bidirectional pad for SWDIO required Output enable switchable per cycle. The protocol turns the line around inside one clock period Input pad that can clock logic required SWCLK is externally driven and must reach sequential logic as a clock. The hardest constraint in a fixed harness Live from power-up required A debug port that firmware has to enable cannot debug why the firmware did not run Access control production Two exposed pins give full register and memory access. Either DM authentication or a fuse or lifecycle lock

07

docs.title: Host side
docs.text:
Element Need Note OpenOCD with a riscv target required Plus a target config describing the DTM and work area GDB remote serial protocol required Standard client, no patches A probe speaking the transport required CMSIS-DAP for SWD. Validated here with MCU-Link and Black Magic Probe

04 · Division of labour

docs.title: What this project supplies, and what you already have.
docs.text:
Layer Supplied by Detail 01 Transport (DTM) this project SwdPhy, SwdDp register file, DMI gateway with clock crossing 02 Debug Module unchanged Existing VexRiscv Debug Module, reached over the same DebugBus 03 Hart support unchanged Debug Mode, debug CSRs and park loop already in the core 04 Triggers unchanged Whatever the core configuration already provides 05 Reset partly this project SWDIO line-reset handling in the transport; system reset unchanged 06 SoC integration this project LiteX --with-swd-debug brings SWDIO out to SoC pins; ElemRV integration merged 07 Host side partly, see caveat OpenOCD gateway and Black Magic Probe support

Open caveat

Upstream OpenOCD does not support a RISC-V target behind an Arm SW-DP. Stock OpenOCD reaches raw-AP; the full RISC-V and GDB path currently needs a fork, as it does for Raspberry Pi. Whether this can be upstreamed rather than carried downstream is an open question and a good reason to talk if you build debug tooling.

05 · Status

docs.title: Merged upstream, running on FPGA, not yet in silicon.
docs.text:
Area Result Upstream Core SWD implementation SWD DTM wired end to end, verified in simulation SpinalHDL #1956, #1966 VexRiscv SWD interface in the core and derivatives #483, #499, #500 VexiiRiscv Same interface in the newer core family #184, #188 LiteX SoC integration --with-cpu-jtag-debug and --with-swd-debug; three-wire SWDIO to SoC pins LiteX #2572, #2669; linux-on-litex-vexriscv #459 Commercial SoC SWDIO exposed on ElemRV elements-nafarr #72, elements-zibal #62 Host tooling Raw-AP on stock OpenOCD; full RISC-V and GDB on a fork; Black Magic Probe support openocd/vexriscv-gateway; Black Magic #2322 Hardware Digilent Arty, MCU-Link CMSIS-DAP probe on a Pmod header. OpenOCD examine, GDB load, break and stepi. JTAG through BSCANE2 for comparison —

Remaining work is the full regression matrix and documentation. Silicon validation on an open process is the next step and is not yet funded.

06 · Evaluation

docs.title: What an evaluation looks like.
docs.text:
The fastest route for a board or SoC team is a LiteX build, because two-wire debug is one flag away.

  • Build a LiteX SoC with --with-swd-debug for your target board.
  • Wire SWCLK and SWDIO to a CMSIS-DAP probe. Two signals and a ground.
  • Run OpenOCD with the supplied target config, then attach GDB.
  • Expect examine to pass, then load, a breakpoint, and stepi to behave as they do over JTAG.

A paid integration for one specific core, board and probe combination is available, with named software revisions, an agreed set of debug operations, acceptance tests, and a separate maintenance arrangement. The RTL stays open under its upstream licences either way.

07 · Questions engineers ask

docs.title: Is this standards-compliant RISC-V debug?
docs.text: It implements the RISC-V Debug Specification with a custom SWD transport. The Debug Module and hart behaviour are per specification. The transport is not, because no ratified version of the specification defines an SWD DTM.

docs.title: Do I have to change my core?
docs.text: No, if it already has a spec-compliant Debug Module and hart-side debug support. Those layers are transport-agnostic. You add a front-end and two pads.

docs.title: Why not just use JTAG?
docs.text: Use JTAG if you have the pins. SWD matters when you do not: two signals instead of four or five, on parts where the pin budget is what forced debug off the chip in the first place.

docs.title: Which probes work?
docs.text: Any CMSIS-DAP probe. Validated with an NXP MCU-Link and with Black Magic Probe, whose firmware now carries support for this path.

docs.title: Does stock OpenOCD work?
docs.text: For raw-AP access, yes. For the full RISC-V target with GDB, not yet. That path needs the fork, which is the same position Raspberry Pi is in.

docs.title: Has it run in silicon?
docs.text: Not yet. Everything above is simulation and FPGA, on a Digilent Arty with a real probe. Silicon validation is the open item, and the honest answer to give an adopter.

docs.title: What does it cost in area?
docs.text: The transport front-end is small. The expensive parts of RISC-V debug are the trigger comparators and, where used, the System Bus Access master, and those are decisions you already made when you chose a core configuration.

docs.title: Is an exposed SWD port a security problem?
docs.text:
Yes, on a production part. Two pins give full register and memory access. Plan for Debug Module authentication or a fuse or lifecycle lock before tape-out, not after.

08 · Contact

docs.title: Where it would help to talk.
docs.text:
Three conversations are worth having: board and SoC teams feeling the pin-count pressure, debug tooling vendors who could help settle the upstreaming question, and education or research groups for whom two wires and a cheap probe is a lower barrier than a JTAG setup.

https://saketsinha.de/VexRiscv-Debug/

docs.title: invoke
docs.text:
Invoke is a Python (2.7 and 3.4+) library for managing shell-oriented subprocesses and organizing executable Python code into CLI-invokable tasks. It draws inspiration from various sources (make/rake, Fabric 1.x, etc) to arrive at a powerful & clean feature set.

  • pyinvoke/invoke: Pythonic task management & command execution.

docs.title: Serve and open
docs.text:
Run mkdocs serve and open browser automatically.

inv serve

Serving on localhost:8000

# set IP and port
inv serve --dev-addr 'localhost:5000'
# set config file
inv serve --config-file ./mkdocs-sample.yml

docs.title: Show all tasks
docs.text:
$ inv --list
Available tasks:

  serve    Serve site and open browser

Show task help.

$ inv serve --help
Usage: inv[oke] [--core-opts] serve [--options] [other tasks here ...]

Docstring:
  Serve site and open browser

Options:
  -c STRING, --config-file=STRING   Provide a specific MkDocs config
  -d STRING, --dev-addr=STRING      IP address and port to serve documentation locally (default: localhost:8000)

Tasks are defined by tasks.py

docs.title: pipenv
docs.text:
Pipenv is a tool that aims to bring the best of all packaging worlds (bundler, composer, npm, cargo, yarn, etc.) to the Python world.

  • pypa/pipenv: Python Development Workflow for Humans.

docs.title: Install all packages
docs.text: pipenv sync --dev  # Installs all packages specified in Pipfile.lock.

docs.title: Run MkDocs
docs.text:
pipenv shell  # Spawns a shell within the virtualenv.
mkdocs serve

Or, run mkdocs with pipenv run

pipenv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: pipenv run
docs.text:
pipenv task are also defined by Pipfile

pipenv run version    # mkdocs --version
pipenv run help       # mkdocs --help
pipenv run inv serve  # inv serve
pipenv run serve      # mkdocs serve
pipenv run build      # mkdocs build
pipenv run deploy     # mkdocs gh-deploy
